children: The International Monetary Fund said on Thursday its policies allow it to bring Senegal's program to its executive board even while the country is discussing debt treatment with its creditors.

No date has yet been set for the executive board to discuss the program, the IMF added. The fund announced on September 1 it reached a staff-level agreement with Senegal for a $2.2 billion, three-year, loan package.
